svg.title: From product direction through seven software lifecycle outcomes
svg.desc: Product direction is separate from software development. The engineering lifecycle progresses from requirements engineering with refine and supporting requirements-engineering, solution design, implementation planning, implementation, verification, release, and operations and evolution. Operations includes incident response, learning and prevention, reliability and signals, and upkeep. Research, documentation, security, and review are shared methods. Technical expertise is selected by engineering capability and accepted stack. Arrows show dependencies and feedback, not required agent invocations or authorization to deploy.

g.text: From product direction to reliable software
One lifecycle, multiple entry points: follow the decisions that are actually needed.
Accepted decisions, contracts, instructions and evidence are reused and updated throughout the lifecycle.
Choose the problem, value, priority and success signal.
Which problem and slice to pursue
Seven outcomes; enter where the work is needed and revisit affected decisions when evidence changes.
Production learning can reopen requirements, design, implementation and product priorities.
Use when relevant; they are not additional sequential phases.
Technical & domain expertise — select by capability and accepted stack
Examples, not fixed dependencies or a privileged framework stack.
Phases describe outcomes, not required skill calls. Authorization, acceptance and verification remain explicit.
